# Pre-registration: Gaia-2 b, MicroObservatory night of 2026-09-26 UT

Scaffold from tools/mobs_night.py, judgment lines edited 2026-09-26 18:15 UTC (git commit time is the authority), committed BEFORE any fit. Build dev165 (723433e).

Frames: 84, 08:13 to 12:22 UT, 60.0 s Clear.
Archive (NEA pscomppars, fetched 2026-09-26 18:14 UTC): P 3.69152240 +/- 3.9e-06 d,
T0 2458843.988750 +/- 1.9e-04, T14 2.721 h, Rp/Rs 0.1248 (depth 1.56%), a/Rs 9.44724214945732,
inc 85.21, e 0.0, Teff 5720.0, V 11.277. Epoch 668: predicted Tmid 2461309.92571 (10:13 UT),
ingress 08:51, egress 11:34; 38 min pre-ingress and 48 min post-egress in the window
(full). Propagated ephemeris bar 4.0 min.

Predictions:
- Sky judged by stars per frame and the target's aperture flux (night_triage), not the background.
  If the counts hold through 08:51-11:34 and the seed target is >200 ADU above background:
  QC PASS. Reasons: all 84 retained frames clear (54/54 in transit), seed target 540 ADU above background
  (floor 200), six comparisons at 1.0-3.0x the target, V 11.3 is brighter than two nights that passed
  (WASP-67 b V 12.5, WASP-11 b V 11.6), predicted scatter/depth 0.53 is better than WASP-67's.
  MARGINAL would not surprise me enough to mean anything; FAIL on this night would.
- Scatter, from the V-magnitude calibration (0.84% at V 11.57 on 2026-09-05, +0.05%/mag from three clean nights, revised 2026-09-18):
  ~0.83%. On a 1.56% depth that is scatter/depth 0.53; with 0.425 giving
  8.2 min at ~3 min cadence, expected Tmid bar ~10 min (range 7-15; two clean nights gave 9.6 and 8.6 against 6.7 and 9.0 predicted, so the bar model is two-point-crude).
  Under 6 min: calibration wrong the other way. Over 18 min: worse night than the counts show.
- THE CLOCK. The archive ephemeris (T0 2019, used in the inits as the fit's prior, as in every calibration row)
  predicts 2461309.92571 (10:13 UT). ExoClock's VERIFIED ephemeris (Kokori et al. 2025, read off the raw page
  2026-09-26: T0 2459726.265491 +/- 9.7e-05, P 3.69153483 +/- 8e-07, 86 observations, recent O-C -0.01 +/- 0.23 min)
  predicts 2461309.93393 +/- 0.5 min (10:25 UT), 11.8 min LATER. Prediction: Tmid within 1 sigma of ExoClock's
  2461309.93393. With a ~10 min bar the night separates the two clocks at only ~1.2 sigma, so it can favour one,
  not decide between them; landing near the archive value would be weak evidence of a problem with this night or
  a prior pulling the fit, not evidence against ExoClock's 86 timings. Landing near ExoClock with the archive in
  the inits is mild evidence the prior does not pull (what the 8-point calibration already suggests).
  More than 3 bars from BOTH clocks: something wrong with the night; it gets the row-57 treatment before any claim.
- Depth within 1 sigma of 1.56-1.63%; Rp/Rs within 1 sigma of 0.1248 (archive, DERIVED from pl_radj/st_rad, not a
  measured ratio) or 0.1276 +/- 0.0051 (Panahi et al. 2022, via ExoClock). The two priors are 0.5 sigma apart; this
  night cannot choose between them.
- If stars-per-frame falls by more than half at any point between 08:51 and 11:34, or the target is under
  ~200 ADU above background in the seed frame: expect FAIL or a rejected night, and the record will say so
  with no depth or timing claim.
- Any printed bar under 0.001 d is a replaced bar (#1401) and gets refit before the ledger.
- First-frame coordinates from a local plate solve; drift by star-pair voting; comps in the triage box within a
  brightness factor of the target; #1409 confirms the rest.
- Not submitted regardless; checkpoint holds.

## Scored (2026-09-26 18:40 UTC; fit finished 18:24, post_run_check: posterior bar, safe to quote)

Result: QC MARGINAL (KTMF 3.74-3.9/5, Delta BIC 92), Tmid 2461309.9310 +/- 0.0025 BJD_TDB (3.6 min bar),
Rp/R* 0.206 +/- 0.027, b 1.011 +/- 0.067, inc 82.6 +/- 2.0, a/Rs 7.84 +/- 0.76, scatter 0.65%.
- QC: PASS predicted, MARGINAL delivered. MISS, of the kind I said would not mean much.
- Scatter: ~0.83% predicted, 0.65% delivered. Better.
- Bar: ~10 min (7-15) predicted, 3.6 delivered: under the 6 min line I set for "calibration wrong the other way".
  Third clean night (WASP-67 b 8.6 vs 13, WASP-11 b 9.8 vs 9.0 aside) saying the V-magnitude bar model is pessimistic.
- Clock: -4.2 min from ExoClock's 2461309.93393 (1.17 sigma: just outside the 1 sigma predicted, a narrow MISS);
  +7.6 min from the archive's 2461309.92571 (2.1 sigma). It favours ExoClock, as the prereg said one night could,
  and with the ARCHIVE value in the inits the fit did not land on its prior: mild evidence the prior does not pull.
- Depth: MISS. (Rp/R*)^2 4.2 +/- 1.1% against 1.56-1.63% (2.4 sigma). Cause visible in the geometry: b 1.01, a grazing
  solution, the same mode as WASP-52 b 09-20 (row 56). The observed dip in the model curve bottoms at ~1.45%,
  consistent with the expected depth; at 0.65% scatter a V-shaped (grazing) and a flat-bottomed (central) crossing
  fit this curve about equally, and the sampler chose grazing, which needs a larger planet for the same dip.
  So: no depth or radius claim from this night. The timing uses the whole symmetric dip and does not depend on
  which geometry was chosen.

parameters.Fit parameter point estimate: Best-fit likelihood point; uncertainties are posterior spread.
parameters.Pre-UltraNest LM boundary scout note: LM solution and covariance envelope were interior after 2 iteration(s).
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline parameter-fit no: Used a0 and a2 from the previous fast UltraNest fit for the full-resolution final run.
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline detrending note: only 19 pre-ingress and 12 post-egress out-of-transit point(s) were available; need more than 12 on each side to fit a linear baseline.
parameters.Sparse posterior live-point extension no: Applied full-resolution selected comparison-star final UltraNest run (200->1200 minimum live points) with fixed a0/a2 from the previous fast UltraNest fit.
parameters.Final residual rejection note: No residual outliers exceeded 3.0 sigma from the iterated median residual (0.0122%, stdev=0.6502%).
parameters.Uncertainty interpretation note: The primary Rp/R* and radius-ratio area-depth uncertainties use model+red-noise when available. The red-noise uncertainty inflates the data-fit standard error by a residual time-binning beta factor before combining it with the model posterior. The flux baseline red-noise uncertainty is the out-of-transit baseline component used for the final-plot baseline band; the transit-depth red-noise uncertainty already includes both the in-transit and baseline terms. The same residual time-binning beta factor is applied to the posterior uncertainties for Tmid, a/Rs, inclination, and impact parameter when reporting their primary model+red-noise uncertainties. The flux-scatter equivalent is also shown as a diagnostic of the full residual scatter around the model.
